    OSCILLA v2.0 Interactive Sound & Frequency Lab

    READY 440 Hz • Sine • Continuous tone • ≤ 2 s • Gain -21.9 dB

    Save preset

    Stored in this browser (localStorage, preset schema v1). The continuous-playback permission is never stored.

    Headphones required

    Binaural beats need one tone per ear: put on headphones and keep the level low before you continue. Speakers mix both channels and the effect disappears.

    Config link

    The clipboard is not available here. Copy the link manually; opening it restores these settings and never starts playback.

    Keyboard shortcuts

    Space (hold)
    Hold to play (programmed patterns: trigger)
    Enter on Hold / Trigger
    Trigger once
    Esc
    Stop immediately; close menus and dialogs
    ← → on tabs and segments
    Move and select
    PgUp / PgDn on the frequency slider
    One octave up / down

    Select, move, delete, duplicate blocks

    Space does nothing while a text field, button or dialog has focus. Start at a low level: OSCILLA caps the logical gain at 0.25 and, unless continuous playback is allowed in Device & Limits, stops every tone after the hard limit.

    About OSCILLA

    — Interactive Sound & Frequency Lab. One static file; runs from file:// and from GitHub Pages; nothing is sent anywhere.

    Signals are digital: sample rate, Nyquist and every spectrum come from the browser's Web Audio API. Levels are relative (dBFS-like), never calibrated sound pressure. Actual speaker and microphone responses are unknown.

    Bundled software: Alpine.js, uPlot (MIT) and p5.js (LGPL-2.1, embedded unmodified); licence texts are in the HTML comment at the top of this file.

    Microphone

    The microphone starts only when you press “Use microphone”. Echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain are requested off, so the analyser sees the raw input. Audio never leaves this page.

    Detected frequencies come from the FFT peak (parabolic interpolation; autocorrelation below 1 kHz) and are never shown finer than the bin resolution. Use the Compare tab for freeze, averaging and peak hold.

    Not a calibrated measurement. From file:// some browsers refuse the microphone; the panel then says so.

    Settings

    Hard limit (Device & Limits): scheduled on the audio clock, so it holds even if the page stalls. It also caps the Finite tone. Other programmed patterns stop at their own end (max 30 s); a continuous sweep repeat needs “Allow continuous playback”.
